members: [untitled BTM module] These genes outline the interface between proliferative arrest and inflammatory secretion that characterises cellular senescence. On the chromatin side, the Polycomb component BMI1 is part of the complex that ubiquitinates histone H2A to silence the CDKN2A locus and keep cells cycling, while the deubiquitinase USP16 removes that mark and opposes it, so the balance between them sets how readily a cell exits the cycle.

[untitled BTM module] This grouping centres on transcriptional repression and chromatin-based silencing, the machinery that keeps developmental and proliferative genes switched off until they are needed. Polycomb components are the anchor: BMI1 is a core subunit of the PRC1 ubiquitin ligase complex that marks histone H2A to maintain silencing, while AEBP2 is a zinc-finger accessory factor that helps target the companion PRC2 methyltransferase to chromatin.

only_in_confusable: [untitled BTM module] These genes mark the resident fibroblast and perivascular stromal compartment of connective tissue, the cell population that builds and remodels extracellular matrix and supplies growth signals to neighbouring epithelium, endothelium and immune cells. Matrix and matrix-associated products such as tenascin C, ECM2, OLFML3 and the BMP antagonist chordin-like 1 shape tissue architecture and the diffusion of morphogens, while locally produced complement components C1S and C7 give stroma a role in innate immune surveillance.

[untitled BTM module] These genes outline a mesenchymal, mechanoresponsive fibroblast programme in which YAP and its paralogue TAZ (WWTR1) convert cytoskeletal tension and matrix stiffness into transcription of matricellular and adhesion genes. CYR61 is a canonical YAP/TAZ target, and alongside collagen III, follistatin-like 1, caveolin-1 and VCAM1 it marks cells that build and remodel connective tissue and support leukocyte and progenitor traffic.

[untitled BTM module] This grouping describes a mesenchymal, fibroblast-like programme in which mechanical and growth-factor cues are converted into matrix remodelling and stromal activation. Its hallmark outputs, the secreted matricellular proteins CCN1 and CCN2, are canonical readouts of YAP/TAZ activity downstream of cell stretch, stiffness and Rho signalling, and caveolin-1 links plasma-membrane mechanics to that response.
